A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InfiniBench. All 16 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support matching the benchmark, experiments, tables, figures, and prompts.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of four models across nine benchmark skills in Tables 2 and 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those evaluations and reports additional model results, human verification outcomes, and qualitative model responses.

M1.justification: The data-collection and question-generation procedures, inputs, skill definitions, and prompt templates are retained. v2 describes the generator as GPT-4o, which was already labeled in v1 Figure 3; this wording update does not establish a changed generation procedure. The human audit validates questions without describing a new filtering or regeneration step.

E1.justification: Both versions use TVQA-derived episodes and MovieNet movies for the same nine skills, reporting 1,219 videos and 108.2K questions. The human audit samples existing questions. MLVU and HowTo100M are discussed as related work, not added evaluation datasets; the revised average duration does not establish changed video coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 expand from four to eight evaluated models, adding GPT-4o, Goldfish, LLaVA-NeXT-Interleave, and MiniGPT4-video. Gemini-Flash 1.5, LLaMA-VID, LWM, and MovieChat remain. This substantially broadens the comparison to additional commercial, retrieval-based, and short-video models.

E3.justification: Appendix A introduces a human-validation protocol with nine annotators and a stated 2.5% sample. Added evaluations use GPT-4o with up to 250 frames, Goldfish with k=3, and short-video models with 8 or 45 frames. Appendix C also revises the stated evaluator from GPT-4 to GPT-4o, although Section 4.1 retains conflicting GPT-4 wording; re-scoring the retained results is not established.

E4.justification: v2 adds a seven-skill human correctness audit, uses short-video models to investigate the benchmark's long-context demands, and presents generation success/failure analyses for linking events and temporal ordering in Figures 15–16. Figures 17–20 add model-response case studies across four skills. These analyses go beyond v1's skill breakdowns and illustrative benchmark questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The new human audit reports sample sizes and point accuracies, without adding uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results, including GPT-4o's 49.16% average accuracy and 3.22/5 score, and Goldfish's 22.57% and 1.77/5 under their respective settings. The original four models' Table 2 scores remain unchanged. New audit results report approximately 92% correctness. The reported average video duration changes from 76.34 to 52.59 minutes, and Gemini's Table 3 global-visual accuracy changes from 31.395 to 31.36, beyond equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theoretical results, proofs, or derivations. The retained skill taxonomy and evaluation explanations do not undergo substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a large, human-centric benchmark covering nine long-video skills. The abstract and conclusion extend the commercial-model findings to GPT-4o and revise the advertised average duration from 76.34 to 52.59 minutes. The claims about benchmark difficulty and the gap between commercial and open-source models remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds substantive explanations involving Goldfish's retrieval and noise filtering, the trade-off between selected clips and whole-video information, and information loss from short-model frame sampling. It also proposes prior movie knowledge as a possible explanation for GPT-4o's performance. The human audit supports a new reliability interpretation. Section 6's source restrictions and transcript-dependence limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds bounded implementation details: GPT-4o's frame/subtitle input sequence, Goldfish's k=3, LLaVA-NeXT-Interleave's eight frames, and MiniGPT4-video's Llama 2 variant with 45 frames. It also specifies Gemini's silent-video and separate-subtitle inputs. Existing generation/evaluation prompts, LWM hardware details, and benchmark access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of HowTo100M and concurrent MLVU, a MLVU row in Table 1, and references to GPT-4o, Goldfish, and LLaVA-NeXT-Interleave. It removes the assertion that InfiniBench is the only benchmark containing very long videos, while retaining its broader scale-and-duration positioning. Existing model-related discussion is moved into Appendix B rather than removed.

P1.justification: The benchmark narrative is substantially reorganized: data collection precedes skill definitions, model-related discussion and evaluation settings are consolidated in Appendix B, and the main results discussion is extensively revised. The appendix is reorganized around verification, evaluation details, examples, failure cases, qualitative results, and the retained generation prompts.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 expand to eight model rows, and v2 adds human-verification and dataset-total tables. Figures 13–20 introduce additional benchmark examples, generation-error illustrations, and qualitative comparisons. Figure 5 moves from the main text to the appendix, while existing examples and prompt displays are reflowed; v1's generation-prompt Figures 13–17 become v2 Figures 21–25.

improvement.justification: v1 provides no reported correctness audit of its generated questions. v2's nine-annotator audit of 2,310 questions, per-skill correctness results, and explicit generation failures substantially improve assessment of the benchmark's central artifact. Broader model comparisons and the corrected duration further strengthen the paper. Ambiguous evaluator naming and incorrectly ordered temporal-skill ranks in Table 2(d) limit the comparisons, but do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
